resources.title: HTTP/1 to HTTP/2 to HTTP/3 Explained

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Describe the sequence of network events when a client opens a secure HTTPS connection to a service behind a reverse proxy, including how DNS, TCP, TLS, and HTTP fit together.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: If HTTP/2 suffers head-of-line blocking under packet loss, why would QUIC/HTTP/3 improve multiplexing and perceived latency in a global application?
key_evaluation_criteria: Accurately explains DNS resolution and TCP connection establishment
Distinguishes TLS termination and upstream request forwarding at the proxy
Compares HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 trade-offs
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Review packet flow, proxy roles, and protocol differences in connection setup, multiplexing, and congestion handling.

resources.title: SOLID Principles: The Software Architecture Foundation

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: When a new payment provider is added to a system, how do the SOLID principles help avoid frequent edits to existing business logic and reduce regression risk?
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: If an existing class is forced to change every time a new feature is added, which SOLID principle is being violated and what refactoring pattern would you choose?
key_evaluation_criteria: Explains abstraction and dependency direction clearly
Identifies the violated principle and a valid structural fix
Shows how modularity reduces change propagation
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Practice identifying design smells such as shotgun surgery and rigid dependencies before refactoring toward interfaces and policy boundaries.

nodes.name: Relational Data Modeling and ACID Transactions

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how an online banking system can preserve accuracy under concurrent transfers while keeping transaction throughput acceptable, and compare isolation choices for that workload.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: If two transactions both read a balance of $100 and subtract $80, why can a race condition occur under weaker isolation, and what consistency guarantee would you choose in a ledger?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands ACID semantics and transactional boundaries
Explains dirty reads, phantom reads, and lost updates
Recognizes when normalization and indexes improve correctness and performance
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Compare database locking and MVCC strategies, and analyze which isolation level best fits financial systems.

nodes.name: API Design, Contracts, and Integration Patterns

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: When should an organization prefer gRPC for internal services while still exposing REST APIs to external clients, and how do you avoid contract drift across teams?
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why is idempotency essential for payment APIs, and how would you design a POST contract that safely retries without double-charging the customer?
key_evaluation_criteria: Balances protocol choice with compatibility and operational needs
Defines stable contracts, versioning, and error semantics
Explains idempotency and safe retry design in distributed systems
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Review API versioning strategies, gateway throttling patterns, and the use of idempotency keys in payment workflows.

nodes.name: Distributed Data Systems and CAP Trade-offs

resources.title: Please Stop Calling Databases CP or AP

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Under a partition event, explain why a distributed system cannot simultaneously guarantee strong consistency and availability, and identify the design trade-off you would make for a global inventory service.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: When a database cluster partitions, how do you decide whether to favor stale reads or write stops and what patterns help reconcile eventual consistency safely?
key_evaluation_criteria: Correctly uses CAP and quorum reasoning
Explains partition and consistency trade-offs
Applies eventual consistency and replication concepts to a real scenario
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Review the formal CAP proof and compare AP, CP, and hybrid designs for global-scale use cases.

resources.title: Kafka Architecture and Internal Log Storage

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: How would you design a reliable order-processing pipeline so an order is saved and the downstream event is published without risking duplicate or missing processing?
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why can a distributed dual-write fail even when each local write succeeds, and how does an outbox pattern avoid inconsistent state across the database and broker?
key_evaluation_criteria: Explains transactional boundaries and message durability
Recognizes idempotency and replay concerns
Describes event ordering, retries, and DLQ handling
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Study local atomicity, outbox relay, and replay strategies for ensuring exactly-once-ish semantics in practice.

nodes.name: Caching, Performance Tuning, and Scalability Patterns

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Design a caching strategy for a read-heavy product catalog whose traffic spikes unpredictably; explain how you handle hot keys, stale data, and backend pressure.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: If a suddenly expired cache key triggers 50,000 concurrent reads, what failure mode is likely and how do you prevent high read amplification from the database?
key_evaluation_criteria: Explains cache invalidation and freshness trade-offs
Recognizes stampede, avalanche, and single-flight remedies
Connects performance issues to backend capacity and queueing
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Think in terms of cache consistency windows, lock coordination, and the role of TTL and distributed lock patterns in reducing load storms.

nodes.name: Microservices Decomposition, CQRS, and Event Sourcing
core_concepts: Event sourcing and immutable event streams

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how you would split a monolithic commerce platform into bounded contexts while preserving query performance, auditability, and correct business behavior across services.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: When a read model requires data from several domain services, why is API composition or materialized views often preferable to a distributed join, and where does CQRS help?
key_evaluation_criteria: Uses bounded context decomposition appropriately
Explains read/write separation and event-powered synchronization
Recognizes operational complexity and trade-offs of microservice ownership
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Review decomposition patterns, event modeling, and the difference between transactional consistency and query optimization.

nodes.name: Containerization, Kubernetes, and Cloud Runtime Design
core_concepts: Kubernetes control plane and worker nodes
Pods, deployments, services, ingress, and autoscaling
Resource requests, limits, and node scheduling
Infrastructure as code and declarative deployment

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how Kubernetes schedules a workload across nodes, what role etcd plays in the control plane, and how you would tune resource limits to prevent noisy neighbor issues.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: If a workload is unstable because of memory pressure, what is the difference between requests, limits, and eviction behavior, and how do you prevent a node from starving other critical services?
key_evaluation_criteria: Describes control-plane and worker-node responsibilities
Explains scheduling, persistence, and healthy pod behavior
Understands resource constraints and cluster resilience
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Review cluster topology, node resource management, and the role of cgroups and the OOM killer in pod stability.

resources.title: How JWT Works Under the Hood

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how OAuth 2.0 and OIDC should be applied in a microservices ecosystem to secure both browser users and service-to-service calls without compromising auditability.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: If a JWT is stateless, how do you revoke a token immediately in a system with many distributed services while still keeping identity checks efficient?
key_evaluation_criteria: Distinguishes authentication from authorization
Understands asymmetric signing, token lifetimes, and revocation
Can identify common vulnerabilities and secure transport patterns
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Think about short-lived access tokens, rotateable refresh flows, key distribution via JWKS, and strict validation of upstream trust boundaries.

nodes.name: System Resilience, Reliability Engineering, and Observability
core_concepts: MTTR, RTO, RPO, and service health modeling

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: During a dependency outage, explain how you protect upstream services using circuit breakers, retries, rate limiting, and degradation strategies while preserving a healthy SLO.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: If downstream latency spikes from 50ms to 5s, why does thread-pool exhaustion happen and how do bulkheads or queue backpressure prevent cascading failure?
key_evaluation_criteria: Identifies failure isolation and recovery states
Understands SLOs, SLAs, and error budgets
Explains observability signals for diagnosis and improvement
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Explore how resilience metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, and controlled failure injection reveal hidden dependencies and service saturation points.

nodes.name: Enterprise Architecture, Governance, and Technical Strategy

resources.title: C4 Model for Visualizing Software Architecture

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Draft an architecture decision record for a large-scale migration from a monolithic system to a hybrid cloud-native platform, including the business context, trade-offs, risks, and governance model.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: When stakeholders prioritize speed over robustness, how do you express the engineering cost of technical debt and align architectural decisions with long-term platform health?
key_evaluation_criteria: Communicates trade-offs clearly and concretely
Uses governance, architecture, and documentation frameworks appropriately
Links decisions to risk, cost, and delivery outcomes
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Use ADRs, C4 diagrams, and risk-based decision matrices to communicate architecture quality and organizational alignment.
